top.title: Austin Reaves celebrates the Lakers being able to win big games without Luka Doncic
top.description: Austin Reaves celebrates the Lakers being able to win big games without Luka Doncic originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . In nine games played this season, Luka Doncic has been spectacular for the Los Angeles Lakers . He is averaging a whopping 40.1 points, 7.8 rebounds, and 7.7 assists per game. He has been the primary reason behind the Lakers ' impressive success at the start of the season. Doncic had to sit out the Lakers' Sunday night game against the Detroit Pistons because of back tightness. That is a worrying sign for the Lakers because back injuries are tough to navigate. However, it seems the Lakers managed to push through without their superstar leading the charge. Austin Reaves lauds how the Lakers won a big game without Luka Doncic After losing LeBron James in the summer, the Lakers have pivoted to fully focusing on maximizing Doncic. That has paid off so far, but there are times when he has to sit out games due to a nagging injury he has been dealing with. Sunday was the best example of this because Doncic is currently dealing with back tightness. Thankfully for the Lakers and their fans, they have Austin Reaves leading the charge. He played like Doncic on Sunday, scoring 43 points to lead the Lakers over the Pistons . MORE: Luka Doncic speaks on what he has improved in his game after joining the Lakers It was an impressive performance from the Lakers because the Pistons are one of the best teams in the Eastern Conference. Moving forward, this is a good sign for the Lakers because they have found a way to keep winning without their best player leading the way. "We just stayed calm; you can get sped up in those moments, but we trust what we got on this team. You got to weather the storm, and that's what we did... We got a lot of guys who can play basketball; they play the right way, they play hard, they know their roles, unselfish guys who are ready to step up when their name is called," Reaves said in his post-game interview after beating the Pistons . The Lakers are humming positively this season, and that bodes well for the long season. Of course, it is still early, so they are building the right habits that can help them thrive during the Playoffs in April. At the moment, they are enjoying the process and aiming to keep developing. Hellebuyck returns to Winnipeg as a member of the Devils on Tuesday, and he is expected to face the noise from Jets fans after he demanded a trade and sat out the start of the season until getting his wish with the deal that sent him to New Jersey. "This has been an organizational decision for us that we've debated at length," Devils GM Sunny Mehta said in a statement Sunday. top.description: Undefeated Bahraini standout Magomed Magomedov turned in a night to remember in his ONE Championship debut, and the Dagestani-trained athlete could not be more pleased with how his maiden outing in the world’s largest martial arts organization played out. The 31-year-old improved to a spotless 16-0 with a tough split-decision triumph over Brazilian star Lucas Gabriel in their lightweight MMA clash at ONE Fight Night 49 on Prime Video inside Bangkok’s Lumpinee Stadium, which broadcast live on Friday, November 6. Photo Credit: ONE Championship Stepping onto the global stage in front of millions of fans around the world is a moment most athletes only dream about. But Magomedov did it in the main event of a stacked U.S. primetime card with an unbeaten record to protect. He looked back on a memorable night with plenty to say. Magomedov told onefc.com: “I’m very happy that I got a chance to get a debut in ONE Championship. I was so happy that I got a debut with a very, very good fighter as well. He was very strong. He was on a series of wins. But I knew myself, I knew I could fight him, and I could win.” View this post on Instagram Gabriel undoubtedly lived up to that high praise, but Magomedov’s suffocating pressure dictated the early tempo. He quickly turned the battle into a complex grappling puzzle, dragging his foe to the canvas and grinding away from top position through most of the opening frame. He continued hunting the takedown in round two, even as Gabriel frantically fought his way out of the grappling exchanges. Round three featured a late surge from the Brazilian, who successfully reversed a scramble and landed heavy knees from top control. Magomedov left the ring with his hand raised , though the split verdict gave him firm opinions on the scoring criteria. He said: “I had more positive moments than my opponent. I’m not very sure why I got the split decision, because I feel like the first two rounds were mine, and then maybe he got the last round only. “[But] generally speaking, I think I got the win because of my pressure and dominance. The KHK Dagestan representative is a deeply demanding judge of himself, and he laid out his honest verdict on his first global showing without any sugarcoating. top.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It was another disappointing loss for the Philadelphia Flyers on Sunday, who fell 4-3 in overtime to the Calgary Flames. The Flyers were getting pressed early on, but flipped a switch halfway through the first period. They looked like an unstoppable team that was sticking to and executing a game plan. The Flyers grabbed the lead in the first period, but lost it when the Flames tied it before the intermission. Then, right out of the first intermission, Philly took the lead early in the second period, just to concede it minutes later. A big power-play goal regained the lead for the Flyers before the second break, giving them the lead entering the third period. The Flames amped up the effort and were really doing everything they could to break even. Philly blew the lead while on the power play, giving up a shorthanded goal to blow their third lead. Following the shorty, the Flames were dialed in and had too many high-danger chances to count, but Dan Vladar played out of his mind to keep the Flyers in the game. Then, overtime mistakes cost the Flyers the game once again. It was another game where the Flyers put forward a really solid effort in the first two periods, and ruined it in the third period. Read More: Flyers Blow Another 3rd Period Lead, Fall 4-3 vs. Flames Dan Vladar Stole a Point for the Flyers Dan Vladar was incredible for the Flyers on Sunday. He finished the game with 22 saves on 26 shots, but his night was so much better than that. Dan Vladar quite literally stole a point for the Flyers with his efforts late in the game. After the Flames had tied the game up, they had countless chances to take the lead before regulation was over. More than half of the chances they had should have been scored, but they weren’t. Vladar put the Flyers on his back and kept those pucks out of the net, forcing the game to overtime and stealing a point for the Flyers. It was a point that the Flyers don’t deserve, either. If it weren’t for Vladar, that point is not there. Vladar stood tall when it mattered most, but once again, his team could not get him the win. Owen Tippett Looked More Like Himself If there were any positives to take from the game, it’s that Owen Tippett is starting to look like himself again. top.title: Lakers star Austin Reaves perfectly sums up LA’s win vs. Pistons without Luka Doncic
top.description: Kelley L Cox-Imagn Images Lakers star Austin Reaves perfectly sums up LA’s win vs. Pistons without Luka Doncic appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Austin Reaves carried the Los Angeles Lakers on Sunday, and he made it clear the team never panicked when things got tight against the Detroit Pistons. With Luka Doncic sidelined due to low back tightness, Reaves erupted for a season-high 43 points as the Lakers held off the Pistons 121-116 at Little Caesars Arena. Afterward, he summed up the win in simple terms. “We just stayed calm. You can get sped up in those types of moments, but we trust what we got on this team. You just got to weather the storm sometimes, and that’s what we did. We played a good fourth quarter and got a really big win against a really good team,” Reaves said after the game . Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “You just got to weather the storm sometimes.” Austin Reaves joins @roquitheus after his season-high 43-point night to talk about the #Lakers ’ fourth-quarter response, trust in their depth and stepping up without Luka. 💪 pic.twitter.com/sAJKiDMlRC — Spectrum SportsNet (@SpectrumSN) November 9, 2026 The Lakers had a storm to weather. Los Angeles raced out to a 38-14 lead after the first quarter and led by as many as 26 points. Detroit fought back, cutting the deficit to three in the third quarter behind a hot-shooting bench. The Pistons never led, however, and Reaves and company did just enough down the stretch to close it out. Reaves was nearly flawless. He knocked down 14 of his 27 shots, went 4-of-6 from beyond the arc and a perfect 11-of-11 from the free-throw line. He added five rebounds and four assists while committing just one turnover. He also credited the Lakers’ depth, which was on full display . Walker Kessler posted 12 points and 16 rebounds, while Collin Sexton and Ziaire Williams each chipped in 17 points. “We got a lot of guys that can play basketball. They play the right way, they play hard, they know their roles, and unselfish guys that are ready to step up when their name’s called,” Reaves said. Still, Reaves knows the Lakers will need that same mindset once Doncic returns. “Obviously, when we get Luka back, everybody’s got to have the same mentality. He’s one of the best players in the league, if not the best player in the league, and we got to do what we got to do to help him be successful and our organization be successful,” he said. For Detroit, Daniss Jenkins exploded for 31 points on eight 3-pointers, while Kevin Huerter added 24. The Lakers improved to 10-2 and will wrap up their back-to-back against the Atlanta Hawks on Monday. top.description: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins walks off the field following a 43-36 overtime victory over the Tennessee Titans at Paycor Stadium on November 1, 2026. The Cincinnati Bengals air attack was on full display as Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins had themselves a game for the second straight week. For Higgins, he scored his 50th career touchdown against the Falcons. “Chase, who finished with 155 yards on 10 catches, and Higgins, who scored his 50 th career touchdown, knew right away that Burrow would spin one of his beauties,” Geoff Hobson wrote in a Cincinnati Bengals article. “Behind Ja’Marr Chase’s 142-yard first half, the best half by a Bengals receiver since 1988, and two more touchdowns from wide receiver Tee Higgins , the Bengals flipped the logistics of an overseas trip with their best start of the season as they eased to a 24-10 halftime lead just three days after landing here for two practices.” Joe Burrow Should Be in MVP Conversation Joe Burrow completed 24 of 29 passes for 271 yards, and 3 touchdowns on Sunday. Burrow was feeding off of the Madrid crowd and was in a rhythm all game long. “I love playing in the stadium. It was a great atmosphere. I loved putting on a show for the people of Spain,” Burrow said . “Joe is playing at unbelievably high level right now,” Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said in the Bengals article . “Joe doesn’t force the ball; he takes the ball where it needs to go based on the looks. So that’s just something we’re used to.” Joe Burrow is currently leading the league in completion percentage. If he keeps up this level of play, he could find himself in the MVP conversation when the regular season is over. Chase and Higgins Are the Best WR Duo in the NFL If we look around the league, it’s hard to find another wide receiver tandem as talented as Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. These guys are two number 1 receivers on the same team and they are getting paid accordingly and handsomely. This win against the Falcons marks Cincy’s 4th straight win and they are now tied for 1st place in the AFC North. Though Ja’Marr Chase was the star of this game, Higgins serves as a great compliment. “It was one of my best performances,” Chase said in an ESPN article . “I just was getting good looks all day, honestly. I can say that. Joe was just believing in me on those one-on-one matchups and every time he got the opportunity, he was just feeding me.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Bengals’ Tee Higgins Achieves Career Milestone vs Falcons appeared first on HEAVY .

top.title: Austin Reaves Cleverly Avoids Addressing Viral Pistons Fan Confrontation After 43-Point Game
top.description: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 08: Austin Reaves #15 of the Los Angeles Lakers reacts after a late second half three point basket against the Detroit Pistons at Little Caesars Arena on November 08, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) Austin Reaves led the Los Angeles Lakers to a 121-116 win over the Detroit Pistons tonight while leading the offense in Luka Doncic’s absence . He finished with 43 points, five rebounds, and four assists, shooting 14-27 from the field (51.9% FG) and 4-6 from beyond the arc (66.7% FG). Late in the second quarter, with less than 10 seconds left in the half, Austin Reaves got into a viral courtside confrontation with a fan in the most gentlemanly way possible. While things didn’t seem heated at all, the Lakers guard calmly but firmly spoke to the fan for about a minute. Later, near the end of the game, Austin Reaves drilled the dagger three-point shot to ice the game and turned around and waved goodbye to the same fan he spoke to at halftime. Austin Reaves TRASH TALKS a Pistons fan before drilling a DAGGER and waving GOODBYE to him. https://t.co/8Fu1xxliUU — Deuce World🌃 (@deuceworldx) November 9, 2026 Clearly, that halftime interaction with the fan lingered in his head throughout the game as he channeled it into a clutch performance in the absence of MVP frontrunner Luka Doncic. However, Austin Reaves seemed to pretend he didn’t know what happened when asked about the confrontation and the endgame celebration during the postgame media scrum in the locker room. “I don’t know what you’re talking about,” Reaves said , looking like he was intentionally keeping the details of the incident to himself. NBA fans saw the interaction and the Lakers star’s celebration, and flooded social media with mixed reactions to Reaves using trash talk as fuel to motivate himself to play better. “Learning his trash talk from Luka.” “Luka is rubbing off on him.” “He is him.” “Reaves is waving like he dropped his kid off at school.” “Unlike Doncic, this was actually a friendly response.” “The coldest American white boy in the game.” Austin Reaves continues to prove he can shoulder the Lakers’ offensive responsibilities when Luka Doncic is unavailable. His 43-point explosion, fueled by a little courtside trash talk, further establishes his importance to the team’s championship ambitions. And even with Doncic’s back soreness, the Lakers fans will hope to have their Slovenian superstar back on the floor tomorrow night. The All-Star guard is expected to miss two months after undergoing knee surgery Oct. 29. Darryn Peterson led the Jazz with 26 points and six rebounds. After splitting their first two games of the season, the Jazz have lost eight in a row and sit at the bottom of the Western Conference. The Timberwolves entered the game with the worst free-throw percentage in the league at .648, but they made 27 of 32 from the line Sunday, with Dosunmu going 8 for 8. Owolabi, who is also the convener of PBAT-MOB Aramoko Community Engagement, spoke during an APC voter education exercise and community engagement in Aramoko, Ekiti Central Senatorial District, over the weekend. She also represents the South-West as a member of the North Central Development Commission. Owolabi said voter education was essential to strengthening democracy, particularly in rural communities where inadequate information about electoral procedures could discourage participation or lead to invalid votes. She said available ward-level records for Aramoko I and Aramoko II showed a combined 17,426 registered voters, compared with 4,680 votes reportedly cast during the presidential election. According to her, the figures indicated that approximately 12,746 registered voters did not participate, representing about 73 per cent of the electorate in the two wards. She urged residents to improve their participation in future elections, stressing the need for the community to translate its voting strength into meaningful democratic engagement. Owolabi said the exercise was designed to educate residents on voting procedures, encourage participation and reduce the number of rejected ballots. nigeria.title: Sultan directs Muslims to sight Jumada Assaniya moon Monday

nigeria.title: Fermin brace earns Liga leaders Barcelona 2-1 win at Atletico
nigeria.description: Fermin Lopez struck twice to help Barcelona come from behind to beat Atletico Madrid 2-1 and move three points clear at the top of La Liga. The Spanish champions lead second place Real Madrid, who beat Valencia 3-0 on Saturday, with Atletico third, now five points behind. Giuliano Simeone fired Atletico ahead in a high-octane start, before Lopez pulled Barca level shortly before the interval at the Metropolitano stadium. The 23-year-old Spain international netted the winner after 66 minutes when Lamine Yamal slipped him in. The match started at a fast pace and both teams hit the woodwork in the opening stages. Alvarez, who tried and failed to force a move from Atletico to Barca in the summer, rounded goalkeeper Joan Garcia but could not finish off the chance as the defence blocked his route to goal. From the resulting corner Atletico defender Marc Pubill headed against the crossbar with Garcia beaten. At the other end Pedri crashed a strike against the woodwork after being fed by Barca’s teenage star Lamine Yamal. Atletico took the lead in the 10th minute, slicing Barca’s defence open. Alvarez crossed for Giuliano Simeone to turn home from close range. The game settled down after that pulsating start, although Alvarez came close to scoring Atletico’s second. The Argentine international’s shot was fumbled by Garcia, but the goalkeeper was able to collect the ball quickly afterwards. Yamal blasted into the side-netting from a tight angle with Barcelona not able to click into their top gears. Despite their struggles they went in level at the break, with a goal out of nowhere. Lopez’s path to the box was blocked but the ball bounced loose to the midfielder and he quickly smashed a strike past Jan Oblak. Early in the second half Alvarez lobbed over the crossbar when running in on goal. The forward came to rue the miss when Barcelona took the lead. Yamal played a clever pass through Atletico’s defence and Lopez kept his cool to beat Oblak. It was his seventh league goal in 11 top flight appearances this season. nigeria.title: Seven killed, over 100 injured in Egypt train collision
nigeria.description: At least seven people have been killed and more than 100 injured after two trains collided near Giza, Egypt, causing several carriages to derail and plunge down an embankment. The country’s railway authority said the trains, travelling south from Giza and Cairo, collided in the area between Kafr Ammar and Al-Raqqa stations in Al-Ayyat. Egypt’s President, Abdel Fattah al-Sisi, said he had directed relevant authorities to investigate the circumstances surrounding the accident and ensure that anyone found negligent was held accountable. The public prosecutor’s office warned that the death toll could rise as rescue and recovery operations continued. The government said hospitals in the affected area had been placed on heightened alert to handle the large number of casualties. Health Minister, Dr Khaled Abdel Ghaffar, said victims were receiving treatment for various injuries, including broken bones and head injuries. The Egyptian Red Crescent also deployed personnel to provide emergency assistance and psychological support to victims and their families at the scene. The ministry confirmed that the driver of one of the trains was among those killed in the collision. According to reports, the first train was travelling from Giza to Fayoum when it crashed into the rear of another train heading from Cairo to Aswan, which was stationary on the tracks. Photographs from the scene showed several overturned carriages, with emergency responders and members of the public searching through the wreckage for survivors. Train services between Giza and the Upper Egypt region were suspended as cranes were deployed to remove the damaged trains. The railway authority had yet to announce when services would resume. The crash occurred close to the location of Egypt’s deadliest railway disaster, which happened in February 2002 when a fire engulfed a passenger train travelling from Cairo to Luxor, killing more than 370 people officially, although some estimates put the death toll higher. Two other train accidents in the area in 2009 also claimed dozens of lives. The latest disaster sparked calls on Sunday for Egypt’s transport minister to resign over the recurring railway accidents. Meanwhile, foreign governments and diplomatic representatives expressed condolences and solidarity with Egypt over the tragedy. Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs expressed solidarity with Egypt and wished the injured a speedy recovery. Turkey’s Ambassador to Egypt also conveyed his condolences on X to the victims, their families and the Egyptian people. Agberos are transport touts who collect money from commercial bus drivers and other transport operators at motor parks, bus stops and along roads, often claiming to represent transport unions or park authorities. Speaking during the Lagos Governorship Debate on Sunday, Doherty said powerful interests within the existing transport system had made it difficult for successive governments to tackle the activities of the operators. The debate was organised by the Nigeria Debate Consortium, a coalition of five media organisations: Channels Television, TVC News, The PUNCH, TheCable and Vanguard Newspapers. “Many of us understand this notion of the agbero system that people talk about. There is no political will to deal with that problem,” Doherty said. He argued that meaningful reform of public transportation would require a government that was accountable to residents rather than interests benefiting from the existing arrangement. “We will modernise the transportation system because we will be elected by the people, not by an agbero network,” he said. nigeria.description: Michael Carrick said he expects to “move forward and keep working” as Manchester United manager despite dropping into the Premier League relegation zone. nigeria.description: By Godwin Oritse The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) processed 9,195 Pre-Arrival Assessment Reports (PAARs) and 99,839 Single Goods Declarations (SGDs) between September and October 2026, generating a combined revenue of approximately ₦1.42 trillion. The figures were disclosed during a joint security press briefing at the National Counter Terrorism Centre (NCTC), under the Office of the National Security Adviser, in Abuja. Speaking at the briefing, the National Public Relations Officer of the NCS, Deputy Comptroller Abdullahi Aliyu Maiwada, said the performance reflected the Service’s commitment to facilitating legitimate trade, improving cargo clearance and strengthening revenue generation through digital interventions and collaboration with stakeholders. A breakdown of the figures showed that the Service processed 2,102 PAARs in September and 7,093 in October, bringing the total to 9,195. Similarly, 48,832 SGDs were processed in September, while 51,007 were recorded in October, giving a combined total of 99,839 declarations. In a statement, Maiwada also disclosed that the Service recorded significant progress in export trade facilitation. FinCEN’s order, published as a PDF pending Federal Register placement, finds MEXC a “primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance” under section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act. Thirty days after that Register notice, covered U.S. financial institutions will be barred from any funds transfer — including convertible virtual currency — to or from MEXC. Reuters reported the same cut-off Friday afternoon. Treasury framed the move as part of Operation Economic Outcast. It is not an OFAC sanctions designation: the order says it does not rewrite Bank Secrecy Act duties or OFAC rules, and it is a FinCEN funds-transmittal ban rather than a Section 311 proposed rulemaking. Treasury alleges MEXC facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit flows from May 2021 through May 2026, including nearly $1.5 billion tied to Russian sanctions evasion and about $22 million linked to Iran’s Central Bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ Qods Force. The platform was still processing trades with sanctioned Garantex and successor Grinex as recently as June 2026, more than four years after OFAC designated Garantex, the release says. What the order does — and when The order , signed by FinCEN Deputy Director Jimmy L. Kirby, covers MEXC Global and named affiliates operating outside the United States, including Seychelles-incorporated MEXC Global Ltd / MX Global Ltd, Estonia’s MEXC Estonia OÜ, Switzerland’s GIDA Technology AG and the U.K.’s MXC Global Ltd, plus successors. Covered institutions face civil or criminal penalties for willful violations. Until the Federal Register publishes the notice, the 30-day clock has not started. entertainment.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky , her Spring/Summer 2027 collection, Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis . The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A CYCLE OF GIVING BACK In nature, nothing is wasted, and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back. That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. Adopt a growth mindset In today’s world, flexibility, adaptability and agility are your currencies for greatness. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . In nine games played this season, Luka Doncic has been spectacular for the Los Angeles Lakers . He is averaging a whopping 40.1 points, 7.8 rebounds, and 7.7 assists per game. He has been the primary reason behind the Lakers ' impressive success at the start of the season. Doncic had to sit out the Lakers' Sunday night game against the Detroit Pistons because of back tightness. That is a worrying sign for the Lakers because back injuries are tough to navigate. However, it seems the Lakers managed to push through without their superstar leading the charge. Austin Reaves lauds how the Lakers won a big game without Luka Doncic After losing LeBron James in the summer, the Lakers have pivoted to fully focusing on maximizing Doncic. That has paid off so far, but there are times when he has to sit out games due to a nagging injury he has been dealing with. Sunday was the best example of this because Doncic is currently dealing with back tightness. Thankfully for the Lakers and their fans, they have Austin Reaves leading the charge. He played like Doncic on Sunday, scoring 43 points to lead the Lakers over the Pistons . MORE: Luka Doncic speaks on what he has improved in his game after joining the Lakers It was an impressive performance from the Lakers because the Pistons are one of the best teams in the Eastern Conference. Moving forward, this is a good sign for the Lakers because they have found a way to keep winning without their best player leading the way. "We just stayed calm; you can get sped up in those moments, but we trust what we got on this team. You got to weather the storm, and that's what we did... We got a lot of guys who can play basketball; they play the right way, they play hard, they know their roles, unselfish guys who are ready to step up when their name is called," Reaves said in his post-game interview after beating the Pistons . The AI hardware giant’s board published a statement on Sunday afternoon that states it is “initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.” The New York Times is the source of that reporting . On October 29 it alleged US government intelligence agencies decided to investigate a woman who goes by Alice Huang and/or Huang Le, on grounds she passes intelligence with Beijing. In that story The Times used the term “close relationship” to describe the Nvidia CEO's associations with both Ms Huang and US president Donald Trump. On Sunday the newspaper alleged US authorities believe Alice Huang and Jensen Huang shared a "romantic" relationship. The Times further alleges Ms Huang is a Chinese citizen who worked for a Singapore-based company called Megaspeed that has bought plenty of Nvidia hardware and is suspected of doing so to make it available to Chinese users, either by running inside datacenters or facilitating transport to the Middle Kingdom. The US has for years banned or restricted exports of advanced GPUs to China, partly because it feels Beijing’s armed forces can use them to build systems that will erode America’s military superiority. Any relationship, of any sort, between Jensen Huang and a Chinese intelligence operative would therefore be enormously concerning. The company told The Times that Jensen Huang and Alice Huang just had normal CEO-to-customer-exec chats that were no threat to Nvidia intellectual property or US national security. Shortly after Nvidia’s board published its statement, Huang sent an email to staff that the company made public . “I owe my family and all of you an apology,” the email opens. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am proud and grateful to be an American.” The CEO’s mail, and the Board’s statement, make no allegations about any “close relationship” with Ms. Huang. science.description: null "Starlog" was one of the greatest sci-fi and fantasy magazines ever, and after a 17-year absence, it's being resurrected. The legendary sci-fi mag went dark back in 2009 as part of the wave of popular publications folding due to years of declining readership and subscriptions. But as of Nov. 13, this geek favorite periodical returns as an annual print edition, and it's available for pre-order now. It’s another indication of digital fatigue in the world, and fans of a certain age will recall the pleasure of poring over each colorful issue packed with in-depth interviews, behind-the-scenes photos, TV guides, classic movie retrospectives, book reviews, con news, and VFX features. The triumphant relaunch of "Starlog" magazine happens on Nov. 13, 2026 (Image credit: Fangoria Holdings) "Starlog" launched in 1976, in the pre-" Star Wars " days, under the leadership of editor-in-chief Kerry O’Quinn. It first arrived with artist Jack Thurston's beautiful painted "Star Trek" cover, featuring William Shatner as Captain James T. Kirk and Leonard Nimoy’s Spock, set against the U.S.S. Enterprise near a shimmering black hole. The magazine continued to inform the science fiction community about upcoming sci-fi TV shows and blockbuster Hollywood films for over three decades; I fondly recall reading each informative and entertaining monthly issue cover-to-cover. Just in time to honor its 50th anniversary this year, "Starlog" blasts back into the sci-fi universe with Issue #375 showcasing cover artwork created by Armenian artist Gabriel Yeganyan. Its geek culture legacy, covering iconic franchises like "Star Wars," "Star Trek," and "Alien," will now live on thanks to Fangoria Holdings and io9 co-founder Annalee Newitz, editor-in-chief. Three vintage "Starlog" magazine issues from my personal collection! (Image credit: Jeff Spry) "During its original 33-year run, 'Starlog' documented science fiction as it evolved across film, television, books, technology, and culture," said 'Fangoria's Tara Ansley. "Fifty years after the magazine first launched, the line between science fiction and the real world has become increasingly difficult to separate. That makes this an especially interesting time to bring 'Starlog' back. Technology may change, but the most compelling questions have always been about people: how we live, what we create, and what kind of future we want to build." "Starlog" reloads for its first annual edition after a long hiatus on Nov. 13. You can pre-order the first issue (Issue 375 in continuity) on the Starlog website .

science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 8, 2005: Europe launches Venus Express, its first mission to Venus
science.description: null On Nov. 8, 2005, Europe launched its first mission to Venus. The spacecraft was called Venus Express. Venus is a hothouse planet, one where the atmospheric pressure can easily crush an unprotected spacecraft. Even from orbit, Venus Express had to survive harsh radiation. But the spacecraft lasted for more than nine years. During that time, Venus Express saw a weird vortex swirling around Venus's south pole . It also saw possible signs of active volcanoes . Venus Express also discovered that the planet generates its own auroras . These auroras happen when particles from the sun hit charged particles in the atmosphere. Late in the Venus Express mission, controllers told the spacecraft to dip down into Venus's clouds — even though the spacecraft wasn't designed to do this. It performed well, but eventually it stopped listening to commands. The spacecraft burned up in the atmosphere in January 2015. A Russian Soyuz rocket launches the Venus Express spacecraft to Venus on Nov. 8, 2005.. (Image credit: ESA) Why it mattered Venus Express established ESA as the third world organization to successfully send a probe to study Venus, following the United States and Soviet Union. (Japan's JAXA became the fourth five years later.) "By studying Venus, scientists learn how Earth-like planets change over time," reads a summary of the planet's exploration prepared by The Planetary Society. "Orbital studies [like Venus Express] hint that Venus may have hosted habitable oceans before becoming inhospitable." "By studying Venus, we can learn how Earth-like planets evolve and what shapes planets throughout the galaxy into temperate, lush worlds instead of sweltering hothouses. Venus also helps scientists model Earth’s climate, and may serve as a cautionary tale on how dramatically a planet’s climate can change," wrote the Society. An illustration of the Venus Express spacecraft in orbit around Venus. (Image credit: ESA) ESA returned to Venus in 2018 when BepiColombo, its joint mission with JAXA, used the planet's gravity to redirect its path toward the planet Mercury. Want more space history? science.title: Scientists simulate an Earth without life to help hunt for aliens and inhabited worlds
science.description: A new computer simulation that depicts Earth, or a rocky planet in general, without life is the latest tool in the quest to discover whether or not we are alone in the universe. Life leaves its mark on a planet, particularly its atmosphere, in the form of a mixture of biochemically created gases. Some are obvious, while others can be produced by both biology and geology, meaning that distinguishing a planet that has life from one that does not, solely based on what gases we can detect in its atmosphere, can be difficult. The key is in knowing which atmospheric conditions can be explained without life. To aid in distinguishing between habitable and inhabited planets, planetary scientist Samantha Gilbert-Janizek of the University of California, Riverside, developed a model that simulates the evolution of a rocky planet without life. "The model can help us see how habitable but non-living planets might mimic living planets," Gilbert-Janizek, who was a PhD student at the University of Washington when the research was conducted, said in a statement. Gilbert-Janizek built upon a model previously developed by Washington’s Rory Barnes that simulated the core, mantle, and crust of a planet. This new model pushed the simulation two steps further by incorporating the surface and atmosphere of the planet as well. In all, the model simulates 19 properties of a rocky planet that are not related to life, including the amount of heat a planet receives from its star , the exchange of heat and chemicals from the core to the surface, and the outflow of certain gases from the subsurface. Gilbert-Janizek’s starting point was to simulate the development of Earth had life never arisen here, therefore providing a baseline with which to compare to exoplanets . She ran the simulation from the birth of Earth 4.5 billion years ago to 500 million years into the future. The result was a lifeless world, but one that still had oceans and an atmosphere. "When we interpret observations of an exoplanet’s atmosphere, this tool will help us determine the probability that what we observe indicates life on the surface," said Gilbert-Janizek. An illustration shows the landscape of a primordial Earth before life arose as lightning splits the skies (Image credit: Robert Lea (created with Canva)) What makes the simulation especially useful is its plug-and-play nature. Researchers can simply apply the bulk properties of whichever planet they are studying to the model, and then just let it run. If the result is a planet with an atmosphere that matches what is detected spectroscopically by the James Webb Space Telescope or, in the future, the various extremely large 30-meter-plus ground-based telescopes or NASA’s planned Habitable Worlds Observatory , then we know that planet probably does not have life as we know it. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 7, 1992: NASA launches Mars Global Surveyor, its 1st Mars mission in 20 years at the time, to map the Red Planet like never before
science.description: null On Nov. 7, 1996, NASA launched its Mars Global Surveyor mission. This was the first mission NASA sent to Mars in almost 20 years! The Mars Global Surveyor spacecraft was an orbiter. It transmitted data from NASA's Mars rovers Sojourner , Spirit and Opportunity back to Earth. The spacecraft also did a lot of its own science. It found surface channels on Mars that appeared to have been created by running water. Mars Global Surveyor looked at the south pole of Mars and saw signs of possible climate change. It also saw a mineral called hematite on Mars. Hematite usually forms in water. NASA then sent its Spirit and Opportunity rovers to look for the hematite, and both rovers found it near their landing sites. Mars Global Surveyor survived much longer than expected. But a space maneuver accidentally exposed one of its batteries to the sun, and the spacecraft lost power. It fell silent forever in November 2006 . NASA launches the Mars Global Surveyor to Mars on a Delta II rocket on Nov. 7, 1996. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered As the first successful Mars mission since the two Viking launches in 1975, Mars Global Surveyor ushered in a new era of exploration of the Red Planet, not only through its own contributions to orbit-based science, but by serving a relay for surface-based rovers. As such, it became a primary pipeline for multiple concurrent Mars missions. "The [Mars Global Surveyor] mission overhauled scientists' understanding of Mars by studying the entire Martian surface, atmosphere and interior. Major findings included dramatic evidence that water still flows on Mars in short bursts down hillside gullies, and the identification of water-related mineral deposits leading to selection of a Mars rover landing site for a subsequent mission," read a NASA description of the probe. Mars Global Surveyor sent back more than 240,000 images to Earth during its nine active years. Want more space history? science.title: Send your name to Saturn's moon Titan with NASA's upcoming Dragonfly mission
science.description: null We still may be some time away from sending humans to distant reaches of the solar system, but you can send your name to Saturn's moon Titan, which has the ingredients of life on its surface thanks to NASA's Dragonfly mission. Dragonfly is an SUV-sized nuclear-powered rotorcraft that NASA aims to launch towards Titan in 2028. The agency opened a special events page in late October to allow members of the public to put their name on the spacecraft. The names will be put upon a chip on Dragonfly during the spacecraft's assembly, and all names must be submitted before Jan. 15, 2027. The agency says that the mission has no "ordinary itinerary," as Dragonfly aims to between areas miles (or kilometers) apart after arriving on the surface in 2034. "Nearly a billion miles away, an extraordinary destination awaits. Titan has an atmosphere, rivers and lakes, seasons, sweeping dunes and a landscape rich in organic material," NASA officials wrote in the event page. "Upon arrival in 2034, Dragonfly will fly from place to place on this intriguing world to uncover clues about this remarkable moon, and the chemistry that could help us understand the ingredients for life." Dragonfly will be one of just a few flying crafts on another world, with the first being NASA's plucky Ingenuity mini-helicopter that arrived on Mars along with the still-running Perseverance rover in 2021. Ingenuity was only designed to make five flights, but made it to 72 until its blades were damaged during a landing on Jan. 18, 2024. NASA is now planning a SkyFall mission on Mars that would use three helicopters, and which may launch as soon as late 2028 for the Red Planet. Dragonfly, however, is not the first mission to Titan: that would be Huygens , which operated for just a few hours on Jan. 14, 2005 after deploying from the Cassini spacecraft. Huygens was the first lander on an outer solar system world, and measured Titan's atmosphere and took data from the surface. A mosaic image of Saturn's moon Titan composed of images produced by the Cassini spacecraft. (Image credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona/University of Idaho) For its part, Cassini flew by Titan more than 100 times before the mission concluded in September 2017 , providing valuable long-term data about the moon from above. Dragonfly aims to show the moon from up close for about 3.3 Earth years. Its destinations will include dunes and a young impact crater called Selk, according to NASA. "Dragonfly is expected to make one flight every one to two Titan days, which is called a Tsol and lasts about 16 Earth days," NASA officials added of the mission . Dragonfly will stop at a variety of geologic sites, where it will collect samples of surface material for analysis inside the rotorcraft by a suite of scientific instruments." science.title: Star Wars is experiencing a golden age of video games
science.description: After a tumultuous start to EA's rebooted Star Wars Battlefront series, in 2021 Lucasfilm and Disney decided to open up the development of new Star Wars games by bringing in different publishers and studios under the Lucasfilm Games banner. Now, over five years on, we can confidently say we're entering a new golden era of amazing Star Wars games . With LucasArts' successor calling the shots and coordinating a multitude of projects set in a galaxy far, far away, even EA's latest efforts like Squadrons and the Jedi series have taken bigger and bolder swings. Now, in 2026, the full potential of the Star Wars universe has become clearer with specific releases squarely aimed at niche audiences. It's become clear that future Star Wars games needn't be expensive endeavors full of familiar faces or concepts. Star Wars Zero Company and Galactic Racer 's restrained scope and confidence have been infectious, and, as it turns out, they're already recognized by all the parties involved as double-A success stories . Now this is podracing! (Image credit: Secret Mode) A Burnout-inspired Star Wars racer (created by a bunch of ex-Burnout devs) is a fantastic pitch if you know your video games, but looking at EA's recent and current direction, it's easy to see why it didn't happen under their reign. The original Burnout studio, Criterion, would have been an excellent candidate, but instead they were sent to work in the Battlefield mines. Still, someone was interested in the idea, and the end result is glorious. Fast and furious, Star Wars: Galactic Racer ignores recent racing game trends and bets big on arcade-y vibes, uncomplicated controls, and a high skill ceiling that challenges you with extremely high speeds, tight turns, and unexpected interruptions as other drivers try to ruin your day. The not-so-secret sauce, however, was its runs-based structure, which injects the flexibility and replay value of roguelite games into the more traditional arcade racing structure that older gamers are familiar with. (Image credit: EA) Fully confident in its central gameplay idea and devoid of modern live-service baggage, Fuse Games' debut title makes the most of the Star Wars setting within the restrictions of simply making a fun and engaging Star Wars racer. It's almost the same approach we felt in Zero Company, a turn-based tactical strategy-RPG that comes from the minds of another team of ex-triple-A developers. "Star Wars but XCOM" should've happened earlier, but we're glad it did this year, and, unsurprisingly, it's a banger. science.title: 'I think we will prevail': NASA chief Jared Isaacman on Artemis, China and the new moon race (exclusive)
science.description: null NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman is serious about launching "big rockets" to the moon every single year for the agency's Artemis program. And the new space race with China is fueling that ambition. "I feel good. I feel like we are certainly on a more achievable path to the lunar surface today than where we were before," Isaacman told Space.com. We recently sat down with the NASA chief to discuss the state of the Artemis program , and, off the bat, he made it clear that he's confident in the U.S. space program following the success of April's Artemis II mission around the moon. In fact, just prior to our conversation, it was announced that Artemis II commander Reid Wiseman will become the new deputy director of NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory. But the road from Artemis II's success to crewed lunar landings and, later, a permanent moon base will take a lot of launches of NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) megarocket, Isaacman stressed. "You know, a lot of people, especially in the space community, start getting [into] if the landers are there or not. I don't really care about that right now. What I care about is that we are launching big rockets no less than once a year," he said. "I think that's imperative for NASA to be doing these deep-space human spaceflight missions right now," Isaacman added. "So, we had a great mission in April of '26. We will launch again in '27." That coming launch will be for Artemis III, a crewed mission to low Earth orbit that will test docking procedures between NASA's Orion capsule and one or both of the Artemis program's private lunar landers — SpaceX's Starship and Blue Origin's Blue Moon. "We need to continue to exercise those muscles," he said, referring to SLS liftoffs. "And, honestly, once a year isn't great, either. I mean, I don't think we're going to get back to the early [space] shuttle days, you know, four missions a year. I don't think we're going to get back to where we were with Apollo, but once a year is the minimum … I would testify that to Congress in this role years down the road. "If NASA is going to be doing deep-space missions, complicated missions, [we should] launch at least once a year and get as much out of it as you can for taking the risk and spending the taxpayer dollars and building towards something greater," Isaacman added. "That's what we're doing with Artemis III, and that's what's going to better prepare us for Artemis IV." The mountainous formation rises about 4 kilometers above its surroundings and is located very close to the lunar south pole. Boasting permanently shadowed crater floors that likely contain deposits of water ice and peaks that receive almost continuous sunlight for solar power generation, the south polar region is consider a prime location for the first human settlement on the Moon. In fact , De Gerlache-Kocher massif itself has been considered as a potential landing site for future crewed Artemis missions to the Moon . science.title: SpaceX launches mystery mission for US Space Force in gorgeous sunset liftoff from California (video, photos)
science.description: null SpaceX just launched a classified mission for the U.S. military. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from California's Vandenberg Space Force Base this evening (Nov. 6) at 7:48 p.m. EST (4:48 p.m. local California time; 0048 GMT on Nov. 7), rising into the sky as the sun sank toward the Pacific. The launch kicked off the USSF-432 mission for the U.S. Space Force , which we know little about. Neither SpaceX nor the Space Force told us much about USSF-432 beforehand, and we learned tonight; SpaceX cut its webcast off about 10 minutes into the flight, shortly after the Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth for a landing. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches the USSF-432 mission for the U.S. Space Force from Vandenberg Space Force Base on Nov. 6, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) That touchdown occurred aboard the SpaceX droneship "Of Course I Still Love You," which was stationed downrange in the Pacific Ocean. It wrapped up the eighth flight for this particular booster, which is designated 1095. The Falcon 9's upper stage, meanwhile, continued carrying its mystery payload skyward. It could be headed to low Earth orbit , outside observers speculate. "It is possibly a batch of classified LEO satellites for the USSF's Space Based Sensing and Targeting (SBST) portfolio based on SpaceX's Starshield satellite bus, based on locations of rocket stage drop zones being exact fits with previous Starlink Group 15 launches," NextSpaceflight.com wrote in a mission description . Starlink is SpaceX's LEO broadband megaconstellation, which consists of more than 11,000 active satellites. Starshield is a similar system designed to provide services to the U.S. military and its allies. Starshield satellites are believed to be based heavily on the Starlink spacecraft bus. The Falcon 9's first stage after its landing on Nov. 6, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) Previous Booster 1095 missions GPS-III 8 | 6 Starlink missions USSF-432 was the 119th Falcon 9 launch of 2026, and the 14th national-security flight of the rocket so far this year. The vast majority of Falcon 9 missions in 2026 — more than 70% — have been devoted to building out the Starlink megaconstellation. SpaceX has also launched six other missions this year. Three were operational flights of the company's Falcon Heavy rocket, while the other three were test missions of its next-gen Starship vehicle. SpaceX plans to retire both the Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy shortly after the fully reusable Starship, the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built, is up and running.
